title: Hiking Trails Near Me: Mapped Routes Nearby
description: Find named, mapped hiking routes near a place with Hiking Trails Near Me — from the open map's hiking data, nearest first. Free.
summary_sentence: Results are limited to returned OpenStreetMap records and may omit closer or unmapped places. Confirm details with an authoritative local source.
quick_answer: The tool searches OpenStreetMap for mapped hiking-route relation records around a chosen location, then sorts returned records by straight-line distance. It requests at most 100 records and displays up to 100, so it cannot guarantee the closest result or a complete list. Data, access and opening status can be incomplete or outdated.

faq: What counts as a trail here?
A hiking route recorded in OpenStreetMap — typically a named, often waymarked itinerary made of path segments, recorded by the mapping community.
Does it give trail length and difficulty?
No. The list shows names, representative points and distances to those points; it does not display trail lengths or difficulty.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
You can search for a place instead of using device location. The selected search centre is sent to OpenStreetMap-based services for the lookup.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Trail names and place names vary by language and source; the map's record is one honest dialect.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
Device location is optional. The selected coordinates are sent to Overpass to search; consult the privacy page for provider and site details.
A trail I know is missing.
Unrecorded or recorded since the snapshot — OpenStreetMap can be edited by anyone, and walkers mapping their own routes is how this list grows.
Can it plan the walk itself?
The route exists in the record; your day plan (times, climb) belongs to the Hiking Route Planner with Elevation.
Are these official rights of way?
Not necessarily. A mapped hiking relation does not establish legal access. Check local rights-of-way records and current land-manager notices.
Dog-friendly? Facilities?
The workspace does not display these details. Check with the land manager.
Circular routes specifically?
The workspace shows representative points, not route geometries or a circular-route filter. Check the complete route with another authoritative source.
Winter conditions and closures?
Seasonal closures and conditions live with land managers and local notices. The map finds the route; the mountain decides the day.
